rows.evidence: Q1: Sections III-IV, the authors implemented the SWARM sensor-driven software/hardware system on a 250 ft x 80 ft groundnut farm in Kuppam, India, and tested it for about 1.5 months (end Feb to mid Apr 2006). Q2: Table V and Conclusion, SWARM delivered 490 mm water versus 540 mm under manual irrigation (exact requirement 420 mm), i.e. manual supplied 129% of requirement vs 117% for SWARM, a 12% wastage avoided; urea 37.8 kg vs 39 kg; yield 859 vs 846 kg/ha. Q8: Section III.B and IV, the authors state that the SPAD chlorophyll meter could not be bought so lab chlorophyll readings were keyed in manually to simulate the sensor, that satellite images could not be obtained so a sample image was used, and that the values presented cover only until 11 April with the system still in use (short, single-season test).
rows.notes: Single farm, single crop, one comparison of SWARM versus manual; no replication, no statistics, no dispersion measures. Soil moisture was measured by digital moisture meters to drive scheduling but no moisture data are reported, so Q4 answered no. The 'farm' is a single ~0.19 ha plot split into two sections, treated as a single field rather than above-field scale (Q6 no). Hardware/engineering description dominates the paper; the performance comparison is a brief table without method detail on how manual-system values were obtained.

notes: Conference paper (IEEE 2006), partly OCR-garbled in Table IV and Future Research sections but results table (Table V) is legible. Description of the manual comparison system is minimal.
